chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khas'ami, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Mighty: 'So whoever is forced [by necessity], neither desiring [it] nor transgressing [its limit],' he said: 'The one who transgresses is the hunter of game, and the one who transgresses further is the thief. It is not permissible for them to eat the dead animal if they are forced by necessity; it is forbidden for them just as it is for the Muslims, and they do not shorten the prayer.'

key_terms.الْعَادِي: The one who goes beyond the limit (further transgression)

ai.seo_question: What does 'transgressing' mean in the context of eating dead meat out of necessity?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between 'al-bagi' (the hunter) and 'al-'adi' (the thief), ruling that their consumption of dead meat is forbidden even in necessity because their act is driven by desire or profit rather than pure survival. This interpretation highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the validity of the exception to prohibition depends on the purity of intent, excluding those who exploit necessity for gain. Furthermore, the hadith extends this restriction to their prayer, indicating that such transgressors do not qualify for the concession of shortening prayers (qasr) during travel.
